entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science

entry.title: RPI-Zero: Zero-shot RNA-Protein Interaction Prediction
entry.summary:
In vivo protein-RNA interactions are mapped almost exclusively by CLIP-seq, which profiles one protein in one cell type per experiment and needs a specific antibody; only about 10% of the roughly 2,000 human RNA-binding proteins have been assayed, and the Protein Data Bank holds around 5,000 protein-RNA complexes, a quarter of them ribosomes. Sequence-based prediction could extend coverage to unprofiled, newly discovered, or designed molecules, but existing predictors are not built for that case. One family trains a separate model per protein and cannot move beyond proteins with CLIP data; the other scores pairs but targets a single RNA class.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #databases

entry.title: FoldAbS: Repurposing the Protein Folding Model as a Foundation Encoder for Antibody Screening
entry.summary:
Therapeutic antibody screening requires prioritizing antibody candidates across specificity, affinity, and developability. Current pipelines typically silo these objectives and underuse structural information that governs antibody-antigen recognition. To address these inefficacies, we introduce FoldAbS, a unified supervised screening framework that reconceptualizes protein folding models as frozen foundation encoders, exploiting their internal representations to capture rich sequence, geometric, and interaction dynamics well beyond basic structure prediction.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #infosec

entry.title: PartiDesign: A structure-sequence co-design paradigm for practical all-to-all biomolecules design
entry.summary:
Engineering interactions among biomolecules offers a route to creating new biological functions. Although unified models have advanced biomolecular structure prediction and design, efficient and controllable generation across molecular modalities remains challenging. A key challenge is to couple three-dimensional structure generation with sequence or chemical-identity design across chemically diverse systems.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: OncoSpot enables benchmarking of cancer spatial transcriptomics methods across tumor evolutionary modes
entry.summary:
Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cellquality control
entry.summary:
Motivation: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses Results: We developed Gene and Chromosome Analysis Toolkit (gcat) and It's a scam To Sell Another Single Cell Analysis Method (its_a_scam) for modular processing and quality control of single cell genomic data, freeing users from their reliance on proprietary tools. gcat is a C++ library for parsing genomic data and working with it over genomic coordinates.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #distributed-systems

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #genomics-proteins
